en.title: Move the Token to Balance a and b
en.description:
A token sits at one of the positions 0..N, and the letters lie between adjacent positions. Each step flips the a/b letter the token crosses. Find the minimum number of steps needed to make the counts of the two letters equal, or −1 if it is impossible.

The input protocol, the ranges added by this site, the examples, and the tests were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains the letter string L (1..100, only a/b), and the second line contains start (0..N).
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: moving right across the first a turns the string into baabab, with 3 of each letter; the answer is 1.

Example 2: moving left 5 steps flips indices 1..5, giving abbaba with 3 of each letter; no shorter move balances the letters, so the answer is 5.

Example 3: the total number of letters, 5, is odd, so they cannot be split into equal counts; output −1.
hints: Whether an edge ends up flipped depends only on whether the end point and the start point lie on opposite sides of it; enumerate every end point reached by walking straight left or right and check whether the letter counts balance.
